title.narrative: Central Sichuan Roads Development

description.narrative: The main objective of the Project is to develop an integrated transport system to support sustainable economic development in Sichuan province. Local roads will complement the expressway in bringing benefits to rural residents. The Project will (i) reduce traffic accidents and vehicle operating costs; (ii) improve access between Chengdu and Kunming, two major growth centers in southwestern PRC; (iii) provide additional transport capacity to accommodate growing traffic; (iv) provide improved access to employment, markets, and social services, and (v) develop capacity of local communications bureaus. The Project has the following components: (i) construction of a 244 km, four-lane access-controlled toll expressway from Ya'an to Lugu, including access roads, interchanges with toll stations, tunnels, bridges, administrative stations, and service areas; (ii) upgrading of 678 km of local roads to improve access to poor remote areas, and roadside stations; (iii) construction of four public transport centers; (iv) procurement of equipment for road maintenance, toll collection, surveillance and communications, tunnel operation facilities, vehicle weigh stations, road safety, and office administration; (v) land acquisition and resettlement; (vi) consulting services for construction supervision, road safety audit, monitoring and evaluation, and capacity building, and (v) developing capacity of local communications bureaus for maintenance. The key inputs needed to implement the Project include civil works, consultants, equipment, and staff of the Sichuan Provincial Transportation Department.

title.narrative: Loan 2181: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 17 Jun 2022
Progress Toward Outcome: The expected outcome has been achieved. Details will be presented in the PCR report which is being prepared.
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Sep 2012: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents//34174-013-prc-smr-07.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: 1. The project expressway civil works has 27 subgrade packages and five pavement packages financed by ADB loan. In addition, there are seven buildings packages, six traffic engineering safety packages, four greening and planting packages, and 12 equipment packages financed by domestic funds. Advance procurement action was approved on 11 March 2005. Bidding started in 2006 and subgrade contracts were awarded in 2007. The project expressway commenced construction on 26 April 2007. In comparing with the implementation schedule envisaged at appraisal, the project expressway started construction about 12 months late mainly due to longer bidding and bid evaluation period. Procurement of pavement packages started in March 2009 and contracts were awarded in November 2009. The overall progress of the project basically caught up with the original schedule (the envisaged construction period of the expressway at appraisal was 66 months while the actual one was 60 months). About 90 km expressway sections were completed earlier and were opened to traffic in December 2010. The entire project expressway was opened to traffic on 28 April 2012.
2. The local roads have a total length of 678 km, of which, twenty-three local roads totaling 158 km were partially financed by ADB and were completed in 2007 as access roads for expressway construction, and the rest local roads totaling 520 km were financed by the government, were implemented by county and municipal communications bureaus, and were completed separately from 2009 to 2012. Along these completed local roads, various services and facilities such as bus terminals, fuel stations, garages, health clinics, groceries, postal offices, police stations, restaurants and free markets etc. were established.
3. Equipment and facilities for the project expressway include traffic engineering packages, scenic and plantation packages, tunnel ventilation, lighting and safety packages, traffic monitoring, surveillance and toll collection packages, and building and auxiliaries packages. All packages were financed by domestic funds and procurements followed national competitive bidding procedures from 2009 to 2011. All equipment including weight-based-toll and safety facilities are now operational and function well since the opening of the project expressway.
4. Four public transport centers (one each in Yingjing, Hanyuan, Shimian and Mianning) were designed to class II service level with a handling capacity of 5,000 passengers per day at each center. Respective county communications bureaus guided by the EA were responsible for implementing these centers. Procurement for these four centers followed national competitive bidding procedures approved by ADB. Four transport centers separately commenced construction and rehabilitation during the period of 2009 to 2012. All transport centers have been completed and are now operational.
5. An international consulting firm was engaged to provide 66 person-months consulting services. The consultant was mobilized on 1 March 2007 and worked closely with the IA and national consultants. The IA also engaged 12 domestic consultants to undertake construction supervision and testing of materials and products through six central laboratories. A total of 368 supervision engineers and technicians were fielded in the sites and 75 professionals conducted engineering testing and assessment in laboratories. The cumulative inputs of national consulting services in the field of subgrade works, pavement works, facilities, and central laboratories amounted to 20,856 person-months.
6. A human resource development plan was prepared including 53 person-months overseas training. A total of 15 overseas trainings were conducted from 2009 to 2012. The overseas training groups submitted training reports to ADB. Knowledge acquired was disseminated within the EA and IA. The IA had also conducted 50 person-months training through the Sichuan Communications and Technology Management College to enhance the local communications bureau staff's capacity and skills in road maintenance and traffic management. During the construction period, the IA had conducted on-site trainings for 5,539 staff.
